nodes.name: Ni(OH)₂ electrodeposition on NF
nodes.procedure: Synthesis of Niᵢᴵ -O-Niᵢᴵ by electrodeposition of Ni(OH)₂ on nickel foam substrate.
nodes.source_text: Guided by theoretical predictions, we further synthesized and characterized the Niᵢᴵ⁺ᵟ -O-Coᵢᴵ⁺ᵟ catalyst, including control Niᵢᴵ⁺ᵟ -O-Niᵢᴵ⁺ᵟ, Ni- O-Co, and Ni-II-O-Ni catalysts

nodes.name: Co-doped Ni(OH)₂ electrodeposition on NF
nodes.procedure: Synthesis of Niᵢᴵ -O-Coᵢᴵ by electrodeposition of Co-doped Ni(OH)₂ on nickel foam substrate at optimal Co doping ratio of 1/3.
nodes.source_text: the optimal UOR performance was achieved at a Co doping ratio of 1/3 (Figure S24)

nodes.name: Ni(OH)₂@Ni on CP substrate
nodes.procedure: Synthesis of Niᵢᴵ⁺ᵟ -O-Niᵢᴵ⁺ᵟ with similar structure on carbon paper substrate to eliminate NF substrate interference for XRD analysis.
nodes.source_text: XRD analysis was based on the target catalyst with a similar structure synthesized on a carbon paper (CP) substrate to eliminate the interference of the NF substrate

nodes.name: Two-step CoNi@Co-Ni(OH)₂ electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Two-step electrodeposition process: (1) First deposit CoNi alloy spheres on nickel foam substrate; (2) Then electrodeposit Co-doped Ni(OH)₂ shell (Co:Ni ratio 1/3) forming nanosheet network encapsulating the alloy core. Confirmed by selective etching with concentrated ammonia solution revealing micron-sized CoNi spheres. Uniform distribution of Ni, Co, O confirmed by elemental mapping. 0.272 nm lattice spacing corresponds to β-Ni(OH)₂ (100) plane.
nodes.source_text: Field emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM) revealed uniformly dispersed spherical microstructures were on the nickel foam (NF) substrate... selectively etched the hydroxide component using concentrated ammonia solution, leaving behind micron-sized CoNi alloy spheres... aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM and elemental mapping revealed uniform distribution of Ni, Co, O with 0.272 nm lattice stripe of β-Ni(OH)₂ (100)

nodes.description: UOR chronopotentiometry stability in 1 M KOH with 1 M urea
nodes.source_text: chronopotentiometry measurement of Ni^{II + δ} -O-Co^{II + δ} at 10mA cm^{-2} for 940h, 300mA cm^{-2} for 760h, and 500mA cm^{-2} for 400h in 1 M KOH with 1 M urea... continuously operating for 2100h at the laboratory- and industrial- current densities of 10 - 500mA cm^{-2}

The UOR || HER system achieved a cell voltage of 1.354V at 10mAcm^{-2}... The system also demonstrated excellent long-term stability over 500h at 100mAcm^{-2}... with FE for H_2 production at 100mA cm^{-2} reaching 99.3% (urea)... energy consumption for H_2 production was calculated to be 3.68kWh m^{-3} for urea electrolysis

When tested with actual urine, the system exhibited performance comparable to urea electrolysis, with FE for H_2 production at 100mA cm^{-2} reaching 99.3% (urea) and 98.6% (urine)... 3.74kWh m^{-3} for urine electrolysis

nodes.description: Faradaic efficiency measurement for UOR products
nodes.source_text: The FE of N-products using Ni^{II+δ} -O- Co^{II+δ} anode approached 90% at potentials below 1.42V_{RHE}, including N_2(25%-30%) NO_2^- (~56%) NO_3^- (< 5%). When potentials above 1.52V_{RHE} O_2 production increased, reducing the FE of N-products to ~80%

nodes.characterization_summary: FE-SEM reveals uniformly dispersed spherical microstructures on nickel foam substrate, with each microsphere encapsulated by a network of nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Field emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM) revealed that uniformly dispersed spherical microstructures were on the nickel foam (NF) substrate, with each microsphere encapsulated by a network of nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM and elemental mapping show uniform distribution of Ni, Co, and O, with 0.272 nm lattice stripe corresponding to (100) plane of β-Ni(OH)2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Aberration-corrected High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron (HAADF-STEM) and the elemental mapping revealed the uniform distribution of Ni, Co, and O, with the 0.272 nm lattice stripe characteristic of catalyst edge distribution corresponding to the 100 crystal plane of β-Ni(OH)2.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms β-Ni(OH)2 phase (PDF#14-0117) in all four catalysts; Co doping causes slight shift of β-Ni(OH)2 peaks to lower angles indicating lattice expansion; additional peaks at 44.4°, 51.7°, 76.2° indexed to metallic Co and Ni with intermediate positions suggesting CoNi alloy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis was based on the target catalyst with a similar structure synthesized on a carbon paper (CP) substrate... The crystal phase of β-Ni(OH)2 (PDF#14-0117) was detected in four catalysts. Upon Co doping, the position of the β-Ni(OH)2 diffraction peak slightly shifted toward lower angles... additional XRD peaks at 44.4°, 51.7°, and 76.2° were indexed to metallic Co (PDF#15-0806) and Ni (PDF#04-0850).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge EXAFS shows Ni-O at ~1.5Å and Ni-M (Ni-O-Ni/Co) at ~2.7Å; additional Ni-Ni peak at ~2.0Å in NiII+δ-O-CoII+δ from CoNi alloy; Co K-edge shows Co-O, Co-Co, Co-M coordination; Co doping and CoNi alloy shorten Ni-O and Co-O bond lengths.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier transform (FT) of the Ni K-edge EXAFS spectra of four catalysts revealed two prominent peaks at R+α=∼1.5Å and ∼2.7Å corresponding to Ni-O and Ni-M (Ni-O-Ni/Co) coordination... Similarly, the Co K-edge EXAFS spectra of NiII+δ-O-CoII+δ also exhibited peaks corresponding to Co-O, Co-Co, and Co-M coordination.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(Co) K-edge absorption edge energies in NiII+δ-O-CoII+δ positioned between Ni(Co) foil and NiO(CoO), indicating overall valence state between 0 and +2 due to CoNi alloy influence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The absorption edge energies of Ni(Co) K-edge in NiII+δ-O-CoII+δ were positioned between those of Ni(Co) foil and NiO(CoO), indicating an overall valence state between 0 and +2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p3/2 at ~856 eV and Co 2p3/2 at ~781 eV correspond to NiII and CoII; NiII+δ-O-CoII+δ shows shift to higher binding energy indicating increased surface oxidation state forming NiII+δ/CoII+δ.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS observed Ni2p3/2 and Co2p3/2 orbitals corresponding to NiII and CoII at binding energy of ∼856 eV and ∼781 eV... NiII+δ-O-CoII+δ showed a shift toward higher binding energy, indicating an increase in surface oxidation state.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiII+δ-O-CoII+δ exhibits highest double-layer capacitance Cdl = 4.23 mF cm-2 in CV measurements, indicative of greater electrochemical active sites related to defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: NiII+δ-O-CoII+δ demonstrated the highest double-layer capacitance (Cdl = 4.23 mF cm-2) in cyclic voltammetry (CV) measurements, indicative of a greater number of electrochemical active sites, which may also be related to the increase in defects.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows lowest charge transfer resistances R_CT1 = 0.45 Ω cm-2 and R_CT2 = 3.23 Ω cm-2 for NiII+δ-O-CoII+δ, demonstrating accelerated charge transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: NiII+δ-O-CoII+δ exhibited the lowest R_CT1 (0.45 Ω cm-2) and R_CT2 (3.23 Ω cm-2), demonstrating accelerated charge transfer during electrooxidation and urea oxidation processes.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows NiIII-O peaks at 473 and 552 cm-1 corresponding to γ-NiOOH and β-NiOOH emerging above 1.27 VRHE; peak intensity increases then decreases with potential while urea C-N peak at 1005 cm-1 diminishes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Upon applying a potential exceeding 1.27 VRHE, two distinct Raman peaks of NiIII-O at 473 and 552 cm-1 emerged on the NiII+δ-O-CoII+δ surface, corresponding to γ-NiOOH and β-NiOOH species.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ ATR-FTIR identifies urea vibrations at 1504, 1650, 1700 cm-1 (C-N, N-H, C=O); CNO- intermediate at 2168 cm-1 appearing with increasing potential (red shift to 2159 cm-1 with 15N-urea); CO32- at 1460 cm-1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 4b, the peaks located at 1504, 1650, and 1700 cm-1 can be found, corresponding to the vibration of C-N, N-H, and C=O of urea molecules... a characteristic vibration peak appeared at 2168 cm-1, which was attributed to the CNO- intermediate species.
